title: ab-metric-selection-workshop-notes
summary: Notes and outcomes from the cross-functional workshop on designing the A/B metric selection flow for the Rollouts Console. Focus: make metric selection usable for product/ML engineers, provide sane defaults, and tie metric choices to alerts and automatic fallback triggers.
body:
Purpose
-----
Quick capture of ideas from the metric-selection workshop (1/15/25). Goal: a lightweight flow in Rollouts that helps users pick reliable experiment metrics, visualize expected sensitivity, and wire those metrics to fallback/rollback automation and observability alerts.

Context and problem statement
---------------------------
Current rollout flow expects users to: pick a primary metric string (free text), set percent traffic, and define success criteria. In interviews engineers and PMs reported:
- uncertainty which metric to choose for model quality (latency, token-level perplexity, business KPIs).
- difficulty mapping metrics from internal observability to the rollout console (names differ, metric tags matter).
- fear of misconfiguring thresholds that either never trigger or trigger too often.
- lack of a quick way to preview how a threshold would have behaved on historical data.

Workshop outcomes (high level)
-----------------------------
1) Introduce a guided Metric Picker with three modes: Recommended, Manual, and Observability-Linked.
2) Provide an inline simulation panel (historical preview) that runs selected metric(s) against the last N days and surfaces expected sensitivity / false positive rate.
3) Tie metric selection to two automation outputs: (a) fallback trigger (auto-traffic-rollback) and (b) alerting destination (Slack/pager/email).
4) Add guardrails and sensible defaults for thresholding: use relative change (pct) + minimum absolute delta where appropriate.
5) Build a small library of metric templates (latency P99, token-penalty, semantic-similarity-drop) that non-experts can pick from.

Detailed UX proposals
---------------------
Metric Picker (entry screen)
- Top row: quick toggle between modes: Recommended | Observability-linked | Manual. Default: Recommended.
- Search bar that maps fuzzy names to observability metrics (search matches: name, tag, description).
- Template carousel below search: small cards with one-line intent (e.g., "safety: toxic-word-rate", "latency: p99 (production)"). Cards show typical units and whether baseline is known.

Recommended mode specifics
- Show 3 auto-suggested metrics based on route usage, model type, and prior rollouts. Indicate reasoning: "chosen because high correlation with user-ctr in last 30d".
- Auto-fill threshold suggestions with two presets: conservative (low FP, slower reaction) and aggressive (fast reaction, higher FP). Slider to pick aggressiveness.

Observability-linked mode
- Allow linking to a datasource (Prometheus/CloudMetrics/Datadog). Dropdown of available metrics from the chosen project.
- For each candidate metric, show tag filters (env=prod, model=redwood-v1). Allow preview of the metric time-series inline (mini-sparkline).
- If metric units mismatch expected units, warn the user.

Manual mode
- Free-text metric name + unit + optional tag filter box. Show mock preview only if user provides a sample query.

Threshold editor
- Dual input: relative change (%) and absolute delta. Example UI copy: "Trigger if metric worsens by > X% and absolute change >= Y units over window Z".
- Default window: 5m, 1h, 24h options. Recommend 1h for latency metrics, 24h for quality metrics.
- Confidence slider: increases sample size requirement for triggering (this maps to lookback & bootstrap sample size). We show expected alert frequency estimate below.

Simulation/Preview panel (core new feature)
- Runs the configured metric & threshold against historical 7/14/30 day windows.
- Outputs: estimated trigger rate, distribution of delta when a trigger would have happened, and example timestamps when an automated rollback would have fired.
- Visual: time-series with shaded periods where thresholds would have been breached.
- UI note: simulation on initial save is run async; show a progress indicator and cache results.

Fallback & alerts binding
- After metric + threshold confirmed, prompt: "Bind to automation?" with choices: Auto-roll back traffic | Create alert | Both | None.
- For auto-rollback, require a secondary confirmation flow if the threshold is aggressive. Add a cooldown setting (e.g., 15m/1h) to prevent flapping.
- Alert destinations: Slack channel, PagerDuty service, Ops email. Allow per-destination mute windows.

Operator guardrails and safety
- Require a "dry-run" option that only creates alerts and does not change traffic. Recommend enabling dry-run on first deployment.
- Prevent binding metrics with extremely low sample rates to auto-rollback (show "insufficient data" with suggested throttling/batching).
- Add a "safety budget" visualization: how many automated rollbacks have been consumed against a monthly budget.

Wireframe notes (sketch points for design)
- Left column: metric picker + templates + search.
- Middle: threshold editor + confidence slider.
- Right: simulation/preview with export button (CSV and PDF).
- Small help icon next to each control linking to microdocs.
- Inline tooltips with one-line examples (e.g., "A 10% P99 latency increase is typically noticeable to users").

Backlog grooming (actionable items)
- ROLL-204: Backend: expose metric metadata & sample rates from observability to console API (owner: Daniel) (est 5d).
- WEB-1123: UI: Metric Picker component + search fuzzy matcher (owner: Ethan) (est 8d).
- ROLL-231: Simulation service: bootstrap historical-run job & caching (owner: Sofia) (est 12d).
- ROLL-239: Automation binding UX and cooldown settings (owner: Priya) (est 3d).
- Docs: microdocs and examples for common metrics (owner: Riley) (est 2d).

Open questions / unresolved decisions
- What is the canonical source of truth for metric names? (SRE team suggested using the metrics registry but product wants a UI-friendly alias layer.)
- Should we allow compound triggers (e.g., latency p99 AND token-sim drop)? UX will get more complex; consider an "advanced" editor.
- How aggressive should the conservative preset be for models serving low-volume routes? Need experimental data.
- Data retention / privacy: historical simulation uses aggregated metrics only; confirm with security.

Next steps and owners
- Priya: draft a lightweight spec for the Metric Picker screens + acceptance criteria (due 1/22).
- Daniel: prototype API contract for metric list + sample rate endpoint (due 1/31).
- Ethan & Sofia: pair on an interactive wireframe for demo to product leadership (due 2/5).
- Riley: start a one-page runbook for operators describing the dry-run and cooldown patterns (due 2/2).

Quick acceptance criteria (for MVP)
- Metric Picker shows templates and can search observability catalog.
- Threshold editor supports relative+absolute with window selection.
- Simulation panel runs against 7/14/30 day windows and returns trigger rate estimate within 48 hours of request (async).
- Automation binding created: auto-rollback and Slack alert creation both wired end-to-end in staging.

Notes to self
- Keep the initial surface small; focus on most common metrics (latency and a small set of quality proxies).
- Ship with conservative defaults and make aggressiveness visible (avoid scary red warnings unless user opts-in).
- Plan a follow-up workshop with SRE to align on metric registry integration.

Attachments/References
- Link to the workshop Figma sketches: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/rollouts-metrics-workshop
- Jira board: https://redwood.atlassian.net/boards/43

End of notes.
